strategy.summary: Reproduce the acf missing='drop'/'conservative' bug by building the buggy statsmodels checkout and running the four TestACFMissing tests added in PR 10017 (test_qstat_drop, test_qstat_conservative, test_confint_drop, test_confint_conservative). On the buggy revision they should fail because nobs=len(x) includes NaNs; on the fixed revision (nobs=non-missing count, n=203 in the Stata check) they should pass against results_corrgram.csv.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) for building the Cython extensions
build_commands: python -m pip install -U numpy scipy pandas patsy pytest cython
pinned_because: numpy: no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the context; unpinned, chosen as a current numpy that supports np.random.default_rng (needs numpy>=1.17). This is my choice, not a documented requirement.
statsmodels: no documented constraint; the revision under test is built from the checkout itself, so no version pin is applied. Build is required because the tree contains Cython extensions.
scipy, pandas, patsy, pytest: not named in the context; included as the usual statsmodels test dependencies, not as documented constraints.

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/tsa/tests/test_stattools.py::TestACFMissing::test_qstat_drop, test_qstat_conservative, test_confint_drop, test_confint_conservative (added by the PR diff, which also adds cls.confint_res from results[["acvar_lb","acvar_ub"]] in setup_class)
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision da83c3b8e37f, test_qstat_drop and test_qstat_conservative fail with an AssertionError at DECIMAL_3 (qstat lag 1 about 0.795745 vs Stata 0.400857), and test_confint_drop and test_confint_conservative fail at DECIMAL_8 because the Bartlett half-width is too small (0.098000 vs 0.138590). On the fixed revision all four pass. The transition alone is the success criterion; no printed value is checked.
strategy.numerical_probe: Reproducer: x = concatenate(default_rng(0).standard_normal(200), full(200, nan)); acf(x, nlags=10, qstat=True, alpha=0.05, missing='drop', fft=False); compare lag 1 qstat and confint half-width to the reference values.

input_output_examples.input: x_with_nans = concatenate(rng.standard_normal(200) with seed 0, np.full(200, nan)); acf(x_with_nans, nlags=10, qstat=True, alpha=0.05, missing="drop", fft=False), lag 1

risks: Platform: the defect is pure NumPy/Python arithmetic with no architecture, threading, or sanitizer dependence, so it should transition on any standard Linux or macOS x86_64 build. Nothing here needs a special platform.
The Cython build must succeed on the buggy commit before tests run; a stale build artifact from another revision would invalidate the transition.

Reference values 0.138590 and 0.400857 were hand-computed in the PR and not independently verified in the passages; the test's own reference is results_corrgram.csv (Stata), which is what the transition actually uses.
The truncated reproducer means the exact assertions in the PR body are not fully visible; the test file diff is the authority.

Only the test diff is known; the source fix diff in _stattools.py (varacf 1/len(x) -> 1/nobs in the non-Bartlett branch, plus nobs computation) is described in the context but not shown, so the fixed-revision behaviour of the Bartlett confint path depends on the merged commit containing that change.
The nobs==0 ValueError guard requested by the reviewer is not shown implemented; it does not affect the test transition for the 200-of-400 NaN input.
Passages do not give input dtype; the default float64 from standard_normal is assumed.

oracle.tolerance: assert_almost_equal DECIMAL_3 for qstat tests; DECIMAL_8 for confint tests
oracle.reference_source: results_corrgram.csv (Stata), columns Q1, acvar, acvar_lb, acvar_ub, referenced by the test setup
oracle.why: The reference is an independent Stata computation with n=203 effective observations after one leading NaN is prepended to realgdp (n_raw=204), so the Stata values define the correct nobs.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On da83c3b8e37f, acf uses nobs=len(x)=400 (or 204 in the class setup) including NaNs, so the Bartlett variance and Ljung-Box q-statistic are too small; the qstat assertion compares res_drop[2][:40] to Stata Q1 at DECIMAL_3 and the confint assertion compares centered half-widths to Stata acvar_lb/acvar_ub at DECIMAL_8, both raising AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision nobs equals the non-missing count (203), the qstat and centered confint match results_corrgram.csv within the stated decimals, and all four tests pass.
